# Design

How this app is built: its stack, layout and conventions.
Read it with `AGENTS.md`, which has the working rules and how the app is tested.

*TanStack's own documentation is vendored in this repo under `docs/tanstack/`: the official
`llms.txt` index for TanStack Router (`router.llms.txt`) and TanStack Query (`query.llms.txt`).
Consult it when working with TanStack Router or Query.*

---

## OfficeFloor REST endpoints — routes MUST live under `rest/api/`

Put every domain REST route under `src/main/resources/officefloor/rest/api/` so its path starts
with `/api/`: `SpaConfig` only lets `/api/*` reach the backend, and a non-`/api/` route is swallowed
by the SPA deep-link fallback (it returns `index.html`, not your endpoint). The reference below uses
non-`/api/` example paths for brevity — in this app the `/api/` prefix is required. See
`src/main/resources/officefloor/README.md`.

---

*The following is OfficeFloor's own agent guidance for this stack, included verbatim
from <https://officefloor.net/AGENTS.md>. It is part of the OfficeFloor architecture.*

## OfficeFloor REST endpoints

Applies when adding or changing REST endpoints. This project serves REST through
OfficeFloor Function Injection, **not** Spring MVC controllers: each endpoint is a
pipeline of small function classes wired together in YAML.

- Requires the OfficeFloor Spring Boot starter in the build:
  `officefloor-rest-spring-boot-4-starter` (Spring Boot 4.x) or
  `officefloor-rest-spring-boot-3-starter` (Spring Boot 3.x). Without it these YAML
  files are inert. (Rules below track these starter versions.)
- Define each endpoint as a YAML file under `src/main/resources/officefloor/rest/`,
  named `<path>.<METHOD>.yml` (e.g. `owners/{ownerId}.PUT.yml` → `PUT /owners/{ownerId}`).
- One small function class per step; compose steps with `next:` and `outputs:`.
- Do NOT generate `@RestController`, `@GetMapping` or `@PostMapping`.
- Transactions: `govern: [ transaction ]` on steps, not `@Transactional`.
- Errors: a handler YAML in `officefloor/escalation/`, not `@ControllerAdvice`.

### Worked example — `PUT /owners/{ownerId}`

The whole shape of an endpoint. The sections after this one are the reference.

`src/main/resources/officefloor/rest/owners/{ownerId}.PUT.yml`

```yaml
# First step runs first. Validate before Load so an invalid body is a 400,
# not masked by a 404 for a missing owner.
validate:
  class: com.example.owner.ValidateOwner
  next: load
load:
  class: com.example.owner.LoadOwner
  next: apply
apply:
  class: com.example.owner.ApplyOwner
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: save
save:
  class: com.example.owner.SaveOwner
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: respond
respond:
  class: com.example.owner.RespondWithOwner
```

```java
// One public method each. State moves by Out<T> (set) → @Val (read), matched by type.
public class ValidateOwner {
  public void validate(@RequestBody @Valid OwnerRequest request, Out<OwnerRequest> body) {
    body.set(request); // body read once here; republished for later steps
  }
}
public class LoadOwner {
  public void load(@PathVariable("ownerId") int ownerId, OwnerRepository repository,
      Out<Owner> ownerOut) throws OwnerNotFoundException {
    Owner owner = repository.findById(ownerId);
    if (owner == null) throw new OwnerNotFoundException(ownerId); // handled below
    ownerOut.set(owner);
  }
}
public class ApplyOwner { // @Val yields the stored object, not a copy — mutate in place
  public void apply(@Val OwnerRequest request, @Val Owner owner) {
    owner.setFirstName(request.firstName());
    owner.setLastName(request.lastName());
  }
}
public class SaveOwner {
  public void save(@Val Owner owner, OwnerRepository repository) {
    repository.save(owner);
  }
}
public class RespondWithOwner {
  public void respond(@Val Owner owner, ObjectResponse<OwnerResponse> response) {
    response.send(OwnerResponse.from(owner)); // this step responds; 200 by default
  }
}
```

`src/main/resources/officefloor/escalation/com.example.owner.OwnerNotFoundException.yml`

```yaml
handle:
  class: com.example.owner.HandleOwnerNotFound
```

```java
public class HandleOwnerNotFound {
  public void handle(@Parameter OwnerNotFoundException ex,
      ObjectResponse<ResponseEntity<String>> response) {
    response.send(new ResponseEntity<>(ex.getMessage(), HttpStatus.NOT_FOUND));
  }
}
```

### Step wiring

Each top-level YAML entry is a developer-chosen step name; the first is the entry
point. `class:` names the function. **Give each function class exactly one public
method** — several public methods fail at start-up unless every reference adds
`method:`.

- `next: <step>` — run that step afterwards. This step's return value arrives there
  as `@Parameter T`.
- `outputs: { <name>: <step> }` — conditional branches. Declare a
  `@FunctionalInterface` parameter annotated `@Flow("<name>")` and call it to take the
  branch; not calling it short-circuits.

### Function parameters

Declare only what the step needs; they resolve by role:

- `@PathVariable`, `@RequestParam`, `@RequestBody` — Spring MVC annotations work.
- Spring beans (repositories, mappers, services) — injected by type as normal.
- `ObjectResponse<T>` (`net.officefloor.web.ObjectResponse`) — send the response with
  `response.send(dto)`. This is how a step responds; wrap as
  `ObjectResponse<ResponseEntity<T>>` to set status explicitly.
- `@Parameter T` (`net.officefloor.plugin.section.clazz.Parameter`) — the previous
  step's return value, a `@Flow` argument, or a thrown escalation.

### Passing state between steps — `Out<T>` / `@Val`

Steps do not call each other. Beyond the single `@Parameter` hand-off, publish state
into a variable (`net.officefloor.plugin.variable`):

- Producer declares `Out<T>` and calls `set(...)`; consumer declares `@Val T`.
- Matching is **by type** — two variables of the same type in one pipeline need a
  `@Qualifier` annotation to disambiguate.
- `@Val` yields the same object the producer stored, **not a copy** — so an `Apply`
  step mutates the entity in place and later steps see the change.

### Naming

Verb plus entity: `Load<E>` (fetch by path variable, publishes `Out<E>`, throws when
absent) · `Build<E>` (construct from body) · `Validate<E>` (bind and validate the body,
publish it) · `Apply<E>` (mutate) · `Save<E>` · `Delete<E>` · `RespondWith<E>` (200) ·
`RespondWith<E>Created` (201) · `RespondWithNoContent` (204).

Keep DTOs at the edges — request body in at the first step, response DTO out at the
responder. Steps in between work with entities.

### Request body and validation

- The HTTP body can be read only once: **only one step per pipeline may bind
  `@RequestBody`**. A second binding fails at runtime. When later steps need it, the
  first step publishes it as a variable.
- `@Valid` runs before that step's method body, so step order decides when validation
  happens. Put the validating step first — otherwise a missing id returns 404 before an
  invalid body can return 400.

### Transactions

`govern: [ transaction ]` for writes, `govern: [ readonly-transaction ]` for reads,
listed on **every** step it covers. Both are provided by the starter. Governance spans
the pipeline, so the request commits once at the end.

### Errors

Functions throw; handlers respond. The exception must be **checked** (`extends
Exception`) so it appears in the `throws` clause. Put the handler in
`officefloor/escalation/<fully.qualified.ExceptionClass>.yml`, taking the exception as
`@Parameter` and responding via `ObjectResponse`. Matching is most-specific-first;
anything unmatched falls through to Spring `@RestControllerAdvice`.

### Security

Guard a whole endpoint file with a Spring Security SpEL expression:

```yaml
composition:
  authorize: "hasRole('OWNER_ADMIN')"
```

I made no changes. I read the Java server under `src/main/java/net/officefloor/hq/app/` and the React front end under `src/main/frontend/features/`.

**Important first:** the sheet does not get its figures from the server. The server sends raw people and claims, and the browser works out every number shown (`features/claims/claims.ts`, `features/periods/periods.ts`, `features/rates/rates.ts`). The server has its own copy of the same rules (`Claim.java`, `Late.java`, `Person.java`, `Rollup.java`, `Settings.java`). It uses that copy to fix dues when settling, check thresholds, take statements, close periods and write the audit lines. The two copies have to agree by hand.

## 1. Figures and the rules behind them

### Per claim (`claim-row-<id>`)
- **Shown as stored:** `claim-amount`, `claim-date`, `claim-note`, `claim-status`, `claim-opened-by`, `claim-corrects`, `claim-ref`, `claim-tags`, `claim-batch`, `claim-split-from`, `claim-proofs`, `claim-reminded` (`remindedOn`) and `claim-late-entry`.
- **`claim-number`:** the period number (`<period>-<n>`, or `X-<n>` for no period) if the claim has one, otherwise its number on the sheet.
  - Numbers are given only when a claim is opened (`ClaimStatusChanger.number`), never while it is a DRAFT. A voided claim keeps its number and numbers are never reused.
  - Period numbering applies when `period-numbering-from` is set and the sheet's today is on or after it. The period is the one the claim's **due-by** falls in.
- **`claim-due-by`:** fixed when the claim is added, by `Person.dueBy` → `Holidays.businessDaysAfter`. It is the "terms"-th business day after the claim's date, skipping weekends and holidays.
  - The terms are taken in this order: the person's own `terms`, then the `terms-<grade>` setting for their grade on the claim's date, then the sheet's `terms` (default 14).
  - The due-by changes again only when a holiday is added (`Claims.refixDueBy`), and only for claims that are not SETTLED or VOID and whose due-by is on or after that holiday. Re-dating a claim keeps its due-by.
- **`claim-period`:** the period containing the due-by (`periodOf`).
- **`claim-due`:** `claimDueCents` in the browser, `Claim.due` on the server:
  1. **Figure** (`claimFigureCents` / `Claim.figure`): the `settledDue` if there is one. Otherwise, if the claim is `bound()` (stated and not PENDING), its `statedDue`. Otherwise the amount × the grade's `Rate.on` / `rateOf` for that date.
     - The grade is the one in force on the claim's date (`gradeOn`).
     - A rate applies from its from-date up to its to-date. No rate gives no figure, shown as `n/a`.
  2. **Rounding** (`Late.rounding` / `roundsHalfUp`): half-up if `roundsOn` is before `policy-date`, half-even otherwise. With `policy-date` blank, it compares with the sheet's today.
     - `roundsOn` is the claim's own date, or for a correction the date of the claim it corrects.
     - Rounding is done on the magnitude, so negative amounts round like positive ones.
  3. **Late charge** (`Late.charge` / `lateCents`): added only while the claim is overdue. For each full 30 days past `graceBy`, it adds the `late-pct` in force on that 30-day boundary, applied to the figure plus the charges so far (compounding). Each step is rounded with the claim's rounding.
     - The late charge is never bound by a statement.
  4. **Floor:** the result is at least the `floor` in force on the claim's date (default 1.00).
     - A settled claim or a correction gets neither the late charge nor the floor.
- **`claim-overdue`** (`overdue`): the claim is OPEN or PENDING, not deferred, and `graceBy` is before today. `graceBy` is the due-by plus the `grace-<grade>` days in force on the claim's date.
- **`claim-deferred`:** OPEN, and `deferredUntil` is after the sheet's today. This is worked out in the SQL in `Claims.COLUMNS`. **`claim-deferred-until`:** the date it was last deferred to.
- **`claim-stated`:** the claim was bound by the person's last statement.
- **`claim-log-line`:** one line per status change, showing the status, the user, the sheet's today and the due at that moment (`ClaimLog`).

### Which claims count
- **`Claim.counts`:** OPEN, PENDING or SETTLED, and not deferred.
- **`Person.counts` / `counted`:** on top of that, an OPEN or PENDING claim that is not bound is set aside if it is dated inside one of the person's holds, or if `retiredNow` is true (the sheet's today has reached `retiredFrom`).
  - The Hold javadoc, `HoldPerson` and the `people.ts` comments say only OPEN claims are set aside by a hold, but the code sets aside PENDING ones too.
- **`countedOn(end)`** is used for periods. It judges a claim by the status it had at the end of that day, read from its log (`statusOn`). A claim that was not added yet or is deferred now does not count. The hold and retirement rules above apply only if the claim is still open now.

### Per person (`person-row-<id>`)
- **`person-grade`:** the grade in force on today. **`person-terms`**, **`person-contact`**, **`person-hold`**, **`person-retired`** and **`person-retired-from`** are shown as stored.
  - The person is shown as retired as soon as `retiredFrom` is set. Their claims are set aside only once today reaches that date.
- **`person-claimed`:** the sum of the amounts of their counted claims.
- **`person-due-total`** (`personDueCents` / the Rollup): the sum of the dues of their counted claims, capped at `cap` (`Settings.capped`).
  - It is `n/a` if their grade today has no rate, unless some counted claim has a figure apart from it (`figureApartFrom`). That means the claim is fixed, or its grade on its date gives a figure that is a different grade from today's, or that is dated on or before today.
- **`person-excess`:** how far the uncapped total is above the cap. It is 0.00 when there is no cap, or the total is `n/a` or under the cap.
- **`person-overdue-count`** and **`person-overdue-total`:** the number and the dues of their counted claims that are overdue.
- **`person-aged-0-30`**, **`person-aged-31-60`** and **`person-aged-61`:** the dues of their counted OPEN and PENDING claims, grouped by days from the claim's date to today. A claim dated in the future goes in 0–30.
- **`person-settled-total`** and **`person-open-total`** (`splitDueCents`): the dues of their counted SETTLED claims and of their counted OPEN or PENDING claims. Neither is capped.
- **`person-active`:** yes if they have a counted OPEN or PENDING claim dated within today and the 29 days before it.
- **`person-backing`:** the sum of `settledDue` over their patrons' SETTLED claims dated within today and the 89 days before it (`recentSettledCents`). These are not filtered by "counted".
- **`person-statement-count`**, **`person-stated-total`** and **`person-statement-date`:** from the server (`StatementSummary`). The date is the as-of date, or the sheet's today when the statement was taken.
- **`person-period-<name>-due-total`:** the period's figure for this person (see the periods list below).
- **`person-watched`:** whether the signed-in user watches this person.

### Sheet-wide figures
- **`rollup-claimed-total`:** the sum of everyone's claimed. It is not trimmed.
- **`rollup-due-total`** and **`header-due-total`:** the people's due-totals added up, skipping `n/a`, then `trimmedSum`. When 3 or more people have a figure, the single highest and the single lowest are dropped.
- **`rollup-overdue-total`** and **`header-overdue-total`:** each person's overdue total, combined with `trimmedSum`. **`rollup-overdue-count`** is not trimmed.
- **`rollup-settled-total`** and **`rollup-open-total`:** plain sums, not trimmed.
- **`tag-<tag>-due-total`:** the dues of counted claims carrying the tag. A claim with two tags counts in both, and a row is listed for every tag any claim has ever carried (`tagsEver`).
- **`month-<yyyy-mm>-due-total`:** the dues of counted claims dated in that month.
- **Summary:**
  - `summary-grade-<g>-count`, `summary-grade-<g>-due-total` and `summary-grade-<g>-active` cover people who are not retired, grouped by today's grade. The due total adds up their capped due-totals with no trimming, and `n/a` adds nothing.
  - `summary-status-<S>-count` counts every claim with that status.
  - `summary-void-<reason>-count` counts voids by reason.
  - `summary-period-<name>-due-total` is the period's due total.
- **`header-people-count`:** everyone, retired people included. **`header-claims-<S>-count`:** claims per status.
- **Periods:**
  - `period-due-total` is the live figure: the dues of claims whose **due-by** falls in the period and that pass `countedOn(period.to)`. The comment in `periods.slot.tsx` wrongly says "whose date falls in it".
  - Once the period is closed or soft-closed, it shows the `closedTotal` and per-person totals fixed by `PeriodCloser`. A person added after the close shows 0.00.
  - `period-closed` shows yes, soft or no.
- **`rate-preview-count`** and **`rate-preview-diff`:** the OPEN and PENDING claims on that grade whose due would change under the candidate rate, and the sum of the changes. Bound claims keep their figure.

### Lifecycle, freezing and dates
- **Status moves** (`ClaimStatus.after`): DRAFT→OPEN; OPEN→SETTLED (settle) or PENDING (a clerk's settle above `clerk-limit`); PENDING→SETTLED (approve) or back to OPEN (reject). Any status except VOID can be voided.
- **What gets frozen:**
  - **Settle or approve** freezes `settledDue` at the due as of that moment, including any late charge. If there is no rate, nothing is frozen and the claim stays live.
  - **Re-settle** (steward only) freezes it again at what the claim would be today as an open, unbound claim (`asOpenUnbound`).
  - **Statement** (`TakeStatement`) binds each counted claim to its figure as of now, without the late charge, and unbinds the rest. It records the person's due-total, capped by the `cap` on that day.
    - It can be taken as of a past date from `SheetStates`.
    - A PENDING claim is never bound. Split and reassign unbind a claim. Re-date keeps the binding. `CancelStatement` (steward only) unbinds all of the person's claims.
  - **Period close** freezes the period's totals. **Soft-close** does the same, but claims can still change. A claim added while its period is soft-closed is marked a late entry (audit line `LATE_ENTRY`). **Reopen** drops the frozen totals.
  - **Auto close:** when the sheet's today changes, every open period with to-date + `grace-days` before today is closed.
- **A claim due inside a closed period** (judged by its due-by) cannot be added, edited, locked, have its status changed, be split, re-dated, reassigned, deferred, re-settled, or be given a proof.
- **The sheet's today** (`SheetClock`) drives every date rule. Changing it:
  - writes `SNAPSHOT` lines,
  - releases every claim lock,
  - keeps a copy of the sheet in both `SheetStates` and `SheetSnapshots` (two separate snapshot systems),
  - runs the auto close.
- **A blank claim date** defaults to `entry-date` if set, otherwise today.
- **Dated settings** each keep values by from-date: `clerk-limit`, `cap`, `floor`, `terms`, `terms-<g>`, `grace-<g>`, `late-pct`, `proof-threshold`, `proof-threshold-<g>` and `note-threshold`.
- **Retirement:** a claim may not be dated, re-dated or reassigned to after the person's `retiredFrom`.

### Who may do what
- **Roles** (`Roles.of`): a user with no role set is a clerk. A user lent the steward role (`Delegations`) acts as a steward while today is inside the delegation. Only a user who was given the steward role (not lent it) can delegate.
- **Viewer:** `ViewerGuard` refuses every POST or PUT, except the bulk open and bulk settle (which refuse each claim and report 0) and bulk grade (which grades no one).
- **Archived sheets and the as-of view** refuse every write.
- **Permission matrix** (`perm-<action>`): the default is clerk and steward for open, settle, void and close; steward only for reassign and reopen. Splitting needs the "open" permission.
- **Steward only:** approve, reject (which needs a reason), void a SETTLED claim (only within 7 days of its last SETTLED log line), re-settle, re-date, cancel a statement, archive the sheet.
- **Four eyes:** the user who opened a claim, or last edited it, may not settle or approve it.
- **Other checks:**
  - A deferred claim can't be settled.
  - Settling or approving a claim whose due is above the grade's (or sheet's) `proof-threshold` needs at least one proof. This is checked before the clerk limit.
  - Opening a claim whose due is above `note-threshold` needs a note.
  - While the sheet has void reasons, a void must pick one of them.
- **Editing:** only a DRAFT can be edited, and only while no other user's editor locks it.
- **Corrections:** a negative amount must name a SETTLED claim of the same person by its shown number. A correction gets no floor and no late charge.
- **References:** an external reference must be unique on the sheet, ignoring case.
- **Split:** the split-off amount must be more than 0 and less than the claim's amount.
- **Bulk settle** is all or nothing and gives the settled claims a batch number. Bulk open and bulk reassign go claim by claim.

### Import, quick-add and hold
- **Paste** (`ValidatePaste`): each line is `name,amount,date,note`. Every line is checked before anything is written, so one bad line adds nothing.
  - The name must already be on the sheet. Negative amounts are refused. A note ending in ` #ref` sets the reference, which must be unique on the sheet and within the paste.
  - A claim may not be due in a closed period or dated after the person's retirement.
  - Each line becomes a DRAFT claim, with a late-entry mark if its period is soft-closed.
- **Quick-add:** finds the person by name (ignoring case) or adds them with grade A, then adds a DRAFT claim dated `entry-date` or today, with an amount of 0.00 or more.
- **Hold:** from a from-date (blank means today) to a to-date (blank means it never ends). The person's unbound open claims dated inside the hold drop out of every live total.

- **Hold:** from a from-date (blank means today) to a to-date (blank means it never ends). The person's unbound open claims dated inside the hold drop out of every live total.

## 2. How hard it was to follow

It is scattered and tangled. The due calculation alone runs through `Claim`, `Late`, `Rate`, `Person`, `Settings` and the `Claims` SQL. It is then written a second time in TypeScript (`claims.ts`, `rates.ts`, `periods.ts`), which is what produces the numbers the screen shows. The permission and freezing rules are split across about 15 per-action step classes plus `ClaimStatusChanger` and `ViewerGuard`, and some of the comments no longer match the code (the hold/PENDING rule and the period's "date" vs due-by). A new developer would need to read both languages side by side to trust any one figure.
